title: Heart Palpitations
diagnosis: Possible cardiac arrhythmia or other underlying heart condition
correct_orders: Order a 12-lead ECG to evaluate for any cardiac arrhythmias.
Refer the patient to a cardiologist for further evaluation and management.
should_avoid: Initiate unnecessary invasive procedures at this stage, as the diagnosis is still uncertain.

rationale.Order1: ECG is a non-invasive diagnostic test that can help identify various types of arrhythmias and other cardiac conditions. A referral to a cardiologist ensures proper management and further investigation.
rationale.should_avoid1: Avoiding invasive procedures at this stage helps minimize patient discomfort, potential complications, and reduces unnecessary costs.
rationale.Oxygen: The patient is experiencing heart palpitations, which can potentially be life-threatening. Oxygen is crucial to provide immediate support for any respiratory distress.
rationale.IV access ×2: Immediate IV access is essential for the administration of medications and fluids if necessary.

physical_exam: Heart Palpitations — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
